questions.question: The foremost right among rights to freedom is ________.
questions.option_1: Right to life and personal liberty
questions.option_3: Right to freedom of speech and expression
questions.solution:
Article 21, which guarantees the Right to Life and Personal Liberty, is considered the most fundamental of all freedoms.
  • Scope: No person shall be deprived of their life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.
  • Expansion: The Supreme Court has expanded this right to include the right to privacy, right to clean environment, and right to dignity.

questions.question: The term ‘Parliament’ refers to the ____________.
questions.solution:
The term 'Parliament' refers to the National Legislature of India.
  • Composition: Under Article 79, the Parliament consists of the President and the two Houses: the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) and the Lok Sabha (House of the People).
  • Authority: It is the supreme legislative body of the country.

questions.question: Fundamental Duties were added in the Constitution of India under the leadership of which Prime Minister of India?
questions.solution:
Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution in 1976 under the leadership of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.
  • Amendment: They were introduced via the 42nd Amendment Act during the Emergency.
  • Source: These duties were inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR.

questions.question: The Vice President of India is elected for a period of ______ years.
questions.solution:
The Vice President of India is elected for a fixed term of 5 years.
  • Re-election: A person is eligible for re-election to that office for any number of terms.
  • Resignation: The Vice President can resign before the term ends by writing to the President.

questions.question: The Electricity (Amendment) Bill, 2022 was introduced in Lok Sabha on August 8, 2022. The Bill amends the Electricity Act established in _______.
questions.solution:
The Electricity (Amendment) Bill, 2022 seeks to amend the Electricity Act, 2003.
  • Key Reforms: The bill aims to facilitate non-discriminatory open access to distribution networks and introduce multiple retail providers in the same area.
  • Regulation: It also strengthens the powers of the regulatory commissions.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Right?
questions.solution:
The Right to Vote is a Constitutional/Legal Right (under Article 326) but is NOT a Fundamental Right.
  • Fundamental Rights: These include the Right to Equality, Freedom, Against Exploitation, Religion, Culture/Education, and Constitutional Remedies.
  • Note: Fundamental Rights are justiciable and protected by the Supreme Court directly.

questions.question: In which of the following states was ‘Kudumbashree,’ women-oriented, community--based, poverty-reduction programme implemented?
questions.solution:
'Kudumbashree' is a landmark poverty eradication and women empowerment programme implemented in Kerala.
  • Structure: It operates through a three-tier structure of neighborhood groups, area development societies, and community development societies.
  • Impact: It is one of the largest women's networks in the world.

questions.question: The Centre introduced a new bill called the Criminal Procedure (Identification) Bill 2022. This Bill will repeal the Identification of Prisoners Act which was established in _______.
questions.solution:
The Criminal Procedure (Identification) Bill 2022 was passed to replace the Identification of Prisoners Act, 1920.
  • Expansion: The new law allows police to collect biometric data (fingerprints, iris scans, biological samples) from convicts and arrested persons.
  • Storage: The data is stored by the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) for 75 years.

questions.question: Protection of life and liberty is included under which Article of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
Article 21 provides for the Protection of Life and Personal Liberty.
  • Survival: This article is so vital that it cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency (along with Article 20).
  • Doctrine: It ensures that the state follows a 'due process' or 'procedure established by law' before restricting freedom.

questions.question: Who moved the Objective Resolution that was later adapted as the Preamble of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
Jawaharlal Nehru moved the historic 'Objective Resolution' in the Constituent Assembly on December 13, 1946.
  • Philosophy: It laid down the fundamental principles and philosophy of the constitutional structure.
  • Outcome: This resolution was later modified to become the Preamble of the Indian Constitution.

questions.question: It is the duty of every citizen to uphold and protect the ________, unity and integrity of India.
questions.solution:
It is a Fundamental Duty (Article 51A) of every citizen to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
  • Responsibility: This duty emphasizes that citizens must act in a way that prevents the fragmentation of the nation.
  • Legal Status: While not legally enforceable, they serve as a moral guide for citizens.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Vice President of India is INCORRECT?
questions.option_1: The Vice President is elected for five years.
questions.option_2: Members of State legislatures do not take part in his elections.
questions.option_3: He acts as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
questions.option_4: He can be removed from his office by the President approved through a resolution passed by the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.
questions.solution:
The statement that the Vice President is 'removed by the President' is INCORRECT.
  • Actual Process: The Vice President is removed by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha passed by an effective majority and agreed to by the Lok Sabha.
  • Notice: At least 14 days' notice must be given before moving such a resolution.

questions.question: Which Part of the Constitution of India reflects the Fundamental Duties?
questions.solution:
Part IV-A of the Indian Constitution contains the list of Fundamental Duties.
  • Article: This part consists of only one article, Article 51A.
  • History: It was not part of the original Constitution but was added in 1976.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution separates the judiciary from the executive?
questions.solution:
Article 50 of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) directs the state to separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services.
  • Independence: This separation is vital to ensure that the judiciary remains impartial and free from political pressure.
  • Goal: It prevents the concentration of power in a single branch of government.

questions.question: The ___________ is a set of written rules that are accepted by all people living within a country.
questions.solution:
A Constitution is defined as a set of written rules that are accepted by all people living within a country.
  • Supreme Law: It determines the relationship between the people and the government.
  • Framework: It defines the powers and limitations of various government organs.

questions.question: In which year were the 73rd and 74th amendments passed by the Parliament?
questions.solution:
The 73rd and 74th Amendment Acts were passed in 1992.
  • Local Governance: The 73rd Act dealt with Panchayats (rural) and the 74th Act dealt with Municipalities (urban).
  • Enforcement: They came into effect in 1993, ushering in a new era of decentralized democracy.

questions.question: The Constitution forbids employment of children below the age of ______ years in dangerous jobs like factories and mines.
questions.solution:
The Constitution (Article 24) forbids the employment of children below 14 years of age in factories, mines, or other hazardous work.
  • Total Ban: Newer amendments to the Child Labour Act have effectively banned child labor in all occupations for this age group.
  • Adolescents: Those aged 14-18 are protected from hazardous employment.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct with reference to the election of the President of India?
questions.option_1: The election takes place in accordance with the principle of proportional representation.
questions.option_2: All doubts and disputes in connection with the President's election can be inquired into and decided by both the Supreme Court and the High Courts.
questions.option_3: The President is elected for a period of five years.
questions.option_4: He/She is indirectly elected by the elected MLAs and MPs.
questions.solution:
The statement that 'doubts and disputes can be decided by both Supreme Court and High Courts' is INCORRECT.
  • Jurisdiction: Under Article 71, only the Supreme Court has the authority to inquire into and decide disputes regarding the President's election.
  • Finality: The decision of the Supreme Court is final in these matters.

questions.question: Which are the two most essential rights to a democracy?
questions.solution:
Equality and Freedom are considered the two most essential pillars of a Democracy.
  • Interdependence: Without equality, freedom creates privilege for a few; without freedom, equality becomes forced and stagnant.
  • Preamble: These ideals are prominently featured in the Preamble to the Indian Constitution.

questions.question: The system based on individual leadership is a __________ system.
questions.solution:
A Presidential system is a form of government where the head of government is also the head of state and leads an executive branch that is separate from the legislative branch.
  • Example: The United States of America is a classic example of this system.
  • Accountability: Unlike the parliamentary system, the executive is not responsible to the legislature for its policies.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement is correct?
I. The family welfare programme has sought to promote responsible and planned parenthood on a compulsory basis.
II. The National Population Policy 2000 provides a policy framework for imparting free and compulsory education upto 14 years of age.
questions.solution:
Statement II is correct; the National Population Policy 2000 provides a framework for free and compulsory education up to 14 years.
  • Statement I: This is incorrect because the family welfare programme promotes planning on a voluntary basis, not compulsory.
  • NPP 2000 Goals: It also aims to reduce infant mortality and achieve universal immunization.

questions.question: Which Article deals with the ‘Power of Parliament to amend the Constitution and procedure therefor’?
questions.solution:
Article 368 grants the Parliament the power to amend the Constitution and prescribes the procedure for it.
  • Initiation: It can only be initiated in either House of Parliament, never in State Legislatures.
  • Approval: Most amendments require a special majority (two-thirds of members present and voting).

questions.question: Which special knowledge or practical experience is NOT a condition for being nominated to Rajya Sabha by the President of India?
questions.solution:
To be nominated to the Rajya Sabha, a person must have special knowledge in Literature, Science, Art, or Social Service; Eloquence is NOT a requirement.
  • Nomination: The President nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha.
  • Purpose: This allows eminent persons to contribute to the legislative process without contesting elections.

questions.question: In which of the following cases did the Supreme Court of India pronounce the theory of the ‘Basic Structure’ of the Constitution?
questions.solution:
The 'Basic Structure' doctrine was established by the Supreme Court in the Kesavananda Bharati Case, 1973.
  • Core Concept: It states that while Parliament has wide powers to amend the Constitution, it cannot alter the essential features that form its foundation.
  • Impact: This is considered the most significant judgment in Indian constitutional history.

questions.question: To safeguard public property and to abjure violence is a_______________ in the Indian Constitution.
questions.solution:
Safeguarding public property and abjuring violence is a Fundamental Duty listed under Article 51A(i).
  • Context: It was added to emphasize that citizens must respect state assets and avoid destructive behavior during protests or unrest.
  • Moral Obligation: It reminds citizens that rights come with responsibilities toward the community.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India authorises the President to seek the opinion of the Supreme Court in specific categories of matters?
questions.solution:
Article 143 gives the President the power to consult the Supreme Court on questions of law or fact.
  • Advisory Jurisdiction: This is known as the Advisory Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.
  • Binding Nature: The opinion given by the court is not binding on the President.

questions.question: The Right to Freedom of Religion is contained within which Articles of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The Right to Freedom of Religion is covered under Articles 25 to 28.
  • Article 25: Freedom of conscience and free profession, practice, and propagation of religion.
  • Secularism: These articles ensure that India remains a secular state with no official religion.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India mentions that business in Parliament shall be transacted in Hindi or English?
questions.solution:
Article 120 of the Constitution specifies that business in Parliament shall be conducted in Hindi or English.
  • Mother Tongue: The Presiding Officer may permit a member to address the House in their mother tongue if they cannot express themselves in Hindi or English.
  • State Level: Similar provisions for state legislatures are found in Article 210.
